issue_request: FHIR-17776 was a Published/Persuasive STU3 FHIR-I change request asking to correct Batch Processing Rules text that implied a non-200 response meant the whole batch failed and no batch operations succeeded.
initial_application: The Jira comment cites GH#c78b3c2ffa, and commit c78b3c2ffa8f233d54df948e98c11dcebb0d5f3d replaced the erroneous whole-batch failure sentence in source/http.html with per-entry non-2xx failure wording.
additional_context: source/http.html is the active RESTful API page via source/hierarchy.xml. Later source history only normalized HTTP status-code markup/terminology and changed "operations" to "interactions"; nearby RESTful API rules allow successful entry statuses such as 201 Created, 202 Accepted, and 204 No Content, so the current non-2xx threshold is more correct than narrowing the text to literal 200.
reconciliation: Published an empty no-change audit commit because the current source already conveys the accepted rule and no source edit is needed.

related_jiras.note: A later terminology cleanup changed "operations" to "interactions" in the same sentence without altering the FHIR-17776 batch failure rule.

evidence_items.summary: The active RESTful API page currently says the overall batch HTTP response is 200 OK when the batch is processed correctly and a non-2xx entry status means that entry failed.
evidence_items.learned: The current build source already includes the semantic correction requested by FHIR-17776.
